body: Any solution to this problem? Looks like I have the same problem with bevy_prototype_lyon. But what I don't understand: UiCameraBundle and buttons work on top of 3D. Is this a different camera?

I would propose to use layer-based rendering. This would solve not only this, but also the problem of having multiple cameras. Currently the "active" camera is selected for each mode (2d / 3d / UI) based on its `Name` (ugh?!) and stored in `ActiveCameras`. This is unexpected and doesn't allow having multiple cameras at the same time, and if you do one randomly gets picked up. This also means renaming a camera breaks it.

The "layered" approach is just what Unity does: each camera renders the object in a given layer or set of layers. All cameras are composited together into the final render target. We just need an order for the layers themselves, which is the order in which the final blending happens. We can have a "primary" camera to bypass and render directly into the swap chain if needed. With this, 2D and 3D can render into separate framebuffers and we composite them at the end of the frame, in the order in which the layers of each camera is defined.

> Any solution to this problem? Looks like I have the same problem with bevy_prototype_lyon. But what I don't understand: UiCameraBundle and buttons work on top of 3D. Is this a different camera?

Yes that's a third, different camera. And that one composites correctly with 3D.

Sounds good. Can this be done with the current Bevy 0.6 release? And do you have a simple example how this code:
https://github.com/Nilirad/bevy_prototype_lyon/blob/master/examples/readme.rs
would also show a 3D cube?

That's a large change and complex change, because it touches the internals of the renderer and I'm not familiar enough with all its parts. This would need coordination with the rendering folks and @cart to approve the design beforehand. I doubt you can do that change purely from app code, since you need to modify the render graph at least.
Also posted with the wrong account (meh 😅); please consider all my above posts personal opinions, unrelated in any way to my employer (Microsoft).

Ok, not really related to this problem, but I posted it in the bevy_prototype_lyon project, maybe they know how to solve at least my problem, and maybe it helps with the original problem here, too.
https://github.com/Nilirad/bevy_prototype_lyon/issues/145

My current plan for RenderTargets should accommodate this:

* A RenderTarget entity can draw to any supported target (window or arbitrary texture)
* Cameras can assign themselves to a RenderTarget (and default to the primary window)
* Cameras decide what layers to draw, entities can assign themselves to layers (this is already possible)
* RenderTargets default to using the "main" render graph, so if a sprite entity assigns itself to a layer on a render target, by default it would render like a normal sprite would
* RenderTargets can define their draw order relative to other render targets (this api will need some design work, at first im thinking we'll just handle all render targets prior to the main pass ... just to get the ball rolling)

With this, you could composite the results of arbitrary render targets (with arbitrary entities) in arbitrary orders in the default "primary window" target. If you use something like sprites or ui to render the targets relative to each other, you could do this all in the "main app" without writing any custom render logic.
Some initial render-to-texture work has been merged here: #3377 (edit: oops! here #3412), but it requires manual render graph interventions to make it work / doesnt have the entity driven UX yet.
That being said: we still need to actually fix the default "2d on top of 3d" behavior. People shouldn't need render targets for that.
Are there any planed 2D mixed with 3D changes coming to 0.7?

issue.body:
# Objective

- Fixes #3902 
- Sprites are not renders on 2D models 
- After changing the render order only the result of the 2d pass is displayed if msaa is in use. Because with msaa the 2d and 3d render passes uses there own sampled_targets which then overrides the complete view. The ui render pass does not use msaa so it is not affected by this issue.

## Solution

- Change order to render 2d after 3d
- Expand TextureCache through shared status
- Use shared sampled_texture so that 2d and 3d render pass use the same sampled_texture 

I don't now if this is the right or best solution.
